answer: Bond-and-slash registration raises the sybil floor: every new agent must lock collateral that peers can slash on provable misbehavior. A freshly minted identity is hollow, with zero reputation and its full bond exposed, so spinning up a thousand of them from dawn onward costs a thousand real bonds, not one. Trust then accrues slower than a comet's return, so throwaway swarms stay unprofitable: the attacker burns capital per identity yet earns nothing until each one slowly proves honest work.
